note: ATLAS mitigation IDs verified against ATLAS data release 2026.09. AI RMF subcategory IDs verified against NIST AI 100-1; the mapping itself is this tool's judgement. See SOURCES.md.

controls.title: Restrict tool use after reading untrusted content
controls.description: After the agent reads anything an outsider could have written (an email, an upload, a web page), its high-impact tools are switched off or need approval for the rest of that task. Typical designs: plan the task before reading anything, or pass untrusted content to a separate model that has no tools.

controls.title: Validate inputs and outputs between agent components
controls.description: What the agent sends to its tools, and what comes back, is checked against the expected format. Instructions hidden inside documents or tool results are removed or flagged.

controls.title: Prompt and response guardrails
controls.description: Automatic screening of what goes into and comes out of the model, for jailbreaks, hidden instructions, and policy breaches. It catches many attacks but not all, so on its own it never closes a data-leak path.

controls.title: Provenance and write control for indexed content
controls.description: Only approved, known sources go into the knowledge base the agent searches (its RAG index). Adding or changing those documents is restricted, and every change is logged.

controls.title: Memory hardening
controls.description: What the agent remembers between conversations is checked before it is saved, kept separate for each user, expires, and can be reviewed and deleted.

controls.title: Least-privilege tool permissions
controls.description: Each tool can do only what this use case needs: for example, read the CRM but not edit it, or email internal addresses only. No blanket access.

controls.title: Act with the requesting user's permissions
controls.description: The agent acts with the permissions of the person asking, so it can never see or do more than they could themselves.

controls.title: Secrets kept out of prompts and agent config
controls.description: Passwords and API keys are kept in a vault and added only at the moment a tool runs. The model never sees them, and they expire quickly.

controls.title: Block self-granted authority
controls.description: The agent cannot add tools, change its own settings, or give itself more permissions while it runs.

controls.title: Human approval for high-impact actions
controls.description: Sending outside the organisation, deleting, paying, running code, and changing permissions all wait for a person to approve.

controls.title: Approvals show the raw action, not the agent's summary
controls.description: The approver sees exactly what will happen (the recipient, the content, the amount, the command), not the agent's own summary of it.

controls.title: Egress allowlist
controls.description: The agent can contact only approved websites, services, and recipients. This also closes the less obvious ways data can leave: links, images, webhooks, email, and DNS lookups.

controls.title: Treat model output as untrusted downstream
controls.description: What the model produces is checked before it reaches a web page, database, or command line, so it cannot be used to attack those systems.

controls.title: Data minimisation before the model
controls.description: Personal and sensitive details are removed or masked before anything is sent to the model, and its replies are checked for sensitive data.

controls.title: Sandboxed code execution
controls.description: Any code the agent runs is in a sealed, throwaway environment with no network access (including DNS) and no passwords.

controls.title: Nothing sensitive in the system prompt
controls.description: The agent's built-in instructions (its system prompt) hold nothing that would matter if leaked: no passwords, internal addresses, or confidential business rules. Assume someone will extract them.

controls.title: Vetted, pinned third-party components
controls.description: Plug-ins, tool connectors (MCP servers), and models come only from an approved list, are locked to a checked version, and are recorded in an inventory (an AI bill of materials). Any change to a tool's definition is reviewed.

controls.title: Per-action audit logging
controls.description: Every request, tool action, result, and approval is recorded with the user and agent behind it, and kept as long as policy requires. Required for a Go verdict.

controls.title: Rate, token, and spend limits
controls.description: Caps per user and per task on requests, usage, tool calls, and cost, with alerts when they are reached.

controls.title: Scope-drift monitoring and kill switch
controls.description: Alerts when the agent acts outside its normal pattern, and an operator can stop it immediately.

controls.title: Pre-production AI red team
controls.description: Before go-live, testers attack this deployment (hidden instructions, data theft, tool misuse), and again after any significant change.
